item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":3,"rationale":"The President presently proclaims the trade embargo; its legal consequence arises from the proclamation itself, with paragraphs 2 and 3 defining its operation.","evidence":"Hereby proclaim an embargo upon trade between the United States and Cuba"},{"segment_id":"2","code":3,"rationale":"The President directly prohibits the specified imports as of the stated effective time, so the segment itself creates the legal restriction.","evidence":"Hereby prohibit, effective 12:01 A.M., Eastern Standard Time, February 7, 1962, the importation into the United States"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The President assigns Treasury responsibility for implementing the already-created prohibition and grants discretion to make exceptions, without dictating any particular exception.","evidence":"authorize and direct the Secretary of the Treasury to carry out such prohibition"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The Secretary receives discretion to determine consistency with the embargo and issue regulations as necessary; no specified later legal outcome is mandated.","evidence":"to promulgate such rules and regulations as may be necessary to perform such functions"},{"segment_id":"5","code":2,"rationale":"The President mandates the Secretary of Commerce to maintain through agency administration the specified legally consequential ban on all exports to Cuba.","evidence":"direct the Secretary of Commerce, under the provisions of the Export Control Act of 1949, as amended"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The President grants the Secretary discretionary authority over exceptions without requiring any specified exception or other legal outcome.","evidence":"authorize him, under that Act, to continue, make, modify, or revoke exceptions"}]}
